titulo: Communicating with Confidence in the Digital World
titulo_es: Comunicarse con seguridad en el mundo digital
estandares: Produzco textos digitales adaptados a su propósito y audiencia. Reporto lo dicho por otros y confirmo información con precisión.
competencias: Evitar falsos cognados; confirmar con tag questions; transformar al estilo indirecto; enlazar ideas con conectores; producir y analizar textos digitales y publicitarios.
componentes: Pensamiento crítico, comunicación, colaboración y creatividad.

proyecto.descripcion_es: En grupos, los estudiantes diseñan una campaña digital sobre un tema de interés escolar: un post persuasivo, una reseña, un anuncio y un reporte de las opiniones recogidas usando estilo indirecto.
proyecto.descripcion_en: In groups, students design a digital campaign on a school-related topic: a persuasive post, a review, an ad and a report of the opinions collected, using reported speech.

lecciones.content_es:
Falsos amigos frecuentes

  • actually = en realidad (actualmente = currently)
  • eventually = finalmente (eventualmente = occasionally)
  • sensible = sensato (sensible = sensitive)
  • embarrassed = avergonzado
  • library = biblioteca (librería = bookstore)
  • assist = ayudar (asistir a = attend)
  • realize = darse cuenta (realizar = carry out)
  • support = apoyar (soportar = put up with)
  • advertisement = anuncio (advertencia = warning)

Pares que se confunden

  • lose (perder) vs loose (suelto)
  • affect (verbo, afectar) vs effect (sustantivo, efecto)
  • advice (sustantivo) vs advise (verbo)
  • its (posesivo) vs it's (it is)
  • then (entonces) vs than (que, en comparaciones)
lecciones.content_en:
Frequent false friends

  • actually = in fact (not at present, which is currently)
  • eventually = finally (not occasionally)
  • sensible = having good judgment (not sensitive)
  • embarrassed = ashamed
  • library = where books are lent (a shop is a bookstore)
  • assist = to help (to go to an event is attend)
  • realize = to become aware (to perform is carry out)
  • support = to back someone (to tolerate is put up with)
  • advertisement = an ad (a caution is a warning)

Confusing pairs

  • lose vs loose
  • affect (verb) vs effect (noun)
  • advice (noun) vs advise (verb)
  • its (possessive) vs it's (it is)
  • then vs than

lecciones.content_es:
La regla básica

Oración afirmativa → coletilla negativa; oración negativa → coletilla afirmativa. Se repite el auxiliar; si no hay, se usa do/does/did.

  • You've seen this post, haven't you?
  • She doesn't follow that account, does she?
  • They will publish it, won't they?

Casos especiales

  • I'm right, aren't I?
  • Let's post it, shall we?
  • Open the link, will you?
  • Con nobody, nothing, никто… se usa they o it: Nobody called, did they?
  • Con negativos encubiertos (never, hardly, rarely) la coletilla va en afirmativo: He never replies, does he?

Entonación

Si sube, es una pregunta real; si baja, solo busca confirmación.
lecciones.content_en:
The basic rule

Affirmative sentence → negative tag; negative sentence → affirmative tag. The auxiliary is repeated; if there is none, use do/does/did.

  • You've seen this post, haven't you?
  • She doesn't follow that account, does she?
  • They will publish it, won't they?

Special cases

  • I'm right, aren't I?
  • Let's post it, shall we?
  • Open the link, will you?
  • With nobody, nothing… use they or it: Nobody called, did they?
  • With hidden negatives (never, hardly, rarely) the tag is affirmative: He never replies, does he?

Intonation

Rising intonation makes it a real question; falling intonation only seeks confirmation.

lecciones.content_es:
Qué cambia

Al reportar lo que alguien dijo, el verbo retrocede un tiempo:

  • presente simple → pasado simple: "I work here" → He said he worked there.
  • presente continuo → pasado continuo
  • pasado simple / presente perfecto → pasado perfecto
  • will → would · can → could · may → might · must → had to

También cambian

Pronombres (I → he/she), tiempo (today → that day, tomorrow → the next day, yesterday → the day before) y lugar (here → there, this → that).

say vs tell

say no lleva objeto directo de persona: He said that… · tell sí: He told me that…

Cuando no hay que retroceder

Si lo dicho sigue siendo verdad o el verbo introductorio está en presente: She says she lives in Cali.
lecciones.content_en:
What changes

When reporting what someone said, the verb moves one step back:

  • present simple → past simple: "I work here" → He said he worked there.
  • present continuous → past continuous
  • past simple / present perfect → past perfect
  • will → would · can → could · may → might · must → had to

Other changes

Pronouns (I → he/she), time (today → that day, tomorrow → the next day, yesterday → the day before) and place (here → there, this → that).

say vs tell

say takes no personal object: He said that… · tell does: He told me that…

When no backshift is needed

If what was said is still true or the reporting verb is in the present: She says she lives in Cali.

lecciones.content_es:
Preguntas de sí o no

Se introducen con if o whether y el orden vuelve a ser el de una afirmación:

"Do you follow her?" → He asked if I followed her. (sin do, sin signo de interrogación)

Preguntas con Wh-

Se conserva la palabra interrogativa y se reordena:

"Where do you live?" → She asked where I lived.

Órdenes y peticiones

Se usa tell / ask + persona + to + infinitivo:

  • "Close the app." → He told me to close the app.
  • "Please help me." → She asked me to help her.
  • Negativo: He told me not to share it.

Verbos introductorios útiles

advise, warn, remind, invite, offer, suggest. Ojo: suggest va con gerundio o con that: He suggested posting it / He suggested that we post it.
lecciones.content_en:
Yes/no questions

They are introduced with if or whether, and the order becomes that of a statement:

"Do you follow her?" → He asked if I followed her. (no do, no question mark)

Wh- questions

The question word is kept and the order changes:

"Where do you live?" → She asked where I lived.

Commands and requests

Use tell / ask + person + to + infinitive:

  • "Close the app." → He told me to close the app.
  • "Please help me." → She asked me to help her.
  • Negative: He told me not to share it.

Useful reporting verbs

advise, warn, remind, invite, offer, suggest. Careful: suggest takes a gerund or a that-clause: He suggested posting it / He suggested that we post it.

lecciones.content_es:
Por función

  • Adición: and, also, moreover, furthermore, in addition, besides
  • Contraste: but, however, nevertheless, on the contrary, whereas, although
  • Causa: because, since, as, due to, owing to
  • Consecuencia: so, therefore, thus, as a result, consequently
  • Ejemplo: for example, for instance, such as, namely
  • Orden: first, then, next, finally
  • Resumen: in short, to sum up, overall, in conclusion

Puntuación

  • however, therefore, moreover abren oración y van seguidos de coma: However, the data is clear.
  • but, so, and unen dentro de la misma oración.
  • because of / due to van con sustantivo; because con oración.

Error frecuente

No se combinan although y but en la misma oración, ni because y so.
lecciones.content_en:
By function

  • Addition: and, also, moreover, furthermore, in addition, besides
  • Contrast: but, however, nevertheless, on the contrary, whereas, although
  • Cause: because, since, as, due to, owing to
  • Consequence: so, therefore, thus, as a result, consequently
  • Example: for example, for instance, such as, namely
  • Order: first, then, next, finally
  • Summary: in short, to sum up, overall, in conclusion

Punctuation

  • however, therefore, moreover open a sentence and are followed by a comma: However, the data is clear.
  • but, so, and join inside the same sentence.
  • because of / due to take a noun; because takes a clause.

Common mistake

Do not combine although and but in the same sentence, nor because and so.

lecciones.content_es:
Signos de puntuación

. period o full stop · , comma · ; semicolon · : colon · ? question mark · ! exclamation mark · ' apostrophe · " quotation marks · ( ) brackets o parentheses · - hyphen · — dash · … ellipsis.

Caracteres especiales

# hash · @ at · _ underscore · / slash · \ backslash · & ampersand · * asterisk · % percent sign.

Reglas de puntuación útiles

  • En inglés no hay signos de apertura: ¿ y ¡ no existen.
  • La coma va antes de but cuando une dos oraciones completas.
  • El apóstrofe marca posesión o contracción, nunca plural: photos, no photo's.

Dictar

All lowercase. · Capital M. · No spaces. · Hyphen, not underscore.
lecciones.content_en:
Punctuation marks

. period or full stop · , comma · ; semicolon · : colon · ? question mark · ! exclamation mark · ' apostrophe · " quotation marks · ( ) brackets or parentheses · - hyphen · — dash · … ellipsis.

Special characters

# hash · @ at · _ underscore · / slash · \ backslash · & ampersand · * asterisk · % percent sign.

Useful punctuation rules

  • English has no opening question or exclamation marks.
  • A comma goes before but when it joins two full clauses.
  • The apostrophe marks possession or contraction, never a plural: photos, not photo's.

Dictating

All lowercase. · Capital M. · No spaces. · Hyphen, not underscore.

lecciones.t: Tipos de texto y lenguaje persuasivo
lecciones.content_es:
Tipos de texto

  • article: informa y desarrolla un tema.
  • review: valora un producto u obra y da una recomendación.
  • ad: persuade en pocas palabras, con imperativos.
  • post: informal, breve, busca interacción.
  • report: objetivo, estructurado, con datos.
  • opinion piece: defiende una tesis.

Recursos persuasivos

  • Imperativos: Discover, Join, Try it today.
  • Preguntas retóricas: Tired of waiting?
  • Superlativos: the fastest, the most reliable.
  • Repetición y ritmo de tres: faster, safer, smarter.
  • Pronombre you para acercarse al lector.

Lenguaje descriptivo

Adjetivos precisos, comparaciones y verbos fuertes: a stunning design, twice as fast, it transforms the way you study.

Registro

Un review admite I; un report prefiere pasiva e impersonal: The data was collected…
lecciones.content_en:
Text types

  • article: informs and develops a topic.
  • review: evaluates a product or work and gives a recommendation.
  • ad: persuades in few words, with imperatives.
  • post: informal, short, seeking interaction.
  • report: objective, structured, with data.
  • opinion piece: defends a thesis.

Persuasive devices

  • Imperatives: Discover, Join, Try it today.
  • Rhetorical questions: Tired of waiting?
  • Superlatives: the fastest, the most reliable.
  • Repetition and the rule of three: faster, safer, smarter.
  • The pronoun you to address the reader directly.

Descriptive language

Precise adjectives, comparisons and strong verbs: a stunning design, twice as fast, it transforms the way you study.

Register

A review allows I; a report prefers the passive and the impersonal: The data was collected…

repaso.resumen_es:
Lo esencial del periodo

Comunicarse bien en digital exige precisión léxica (falsos cognados), confirmar (tag questions), reportar lo dicho por otros y enlazar ideas con los conectores adecuados.

Puntos gramaticales

  • Tag: se repite el auxiliar y se invierte el signo; aren't I y shall we son excepciones.
  • Estilo indirecto: el verbo retrocede un tiempo y cambian pronombres, tiempo y lugar.
  • Preguntas reportadas: if / whether y orden de afirmación.
  • Órdenes reportadas: tell/ask + persona + to (o not to).
  • however y therefore abren oración con coma; due to va con sustantivo.

Vocabulario

Falsos amigos, puntuación y caracteres, redes sociales y publicidad, tipos de texto y recursos persuasivos.
repaso.resumen_en:
The core of the term

Communicating well online requires lexical precision (false cognates), confirming (tag questions), reporting what others said and linking ideas with the right connectors.

Grammar points

  • Tag: repeat the auxiliary and flip the polarity; aren't I and shall we are exceptions.
  • Reported speech: the verb shifts back and pronouns, time and place change.
  • Reported questions: if / whether and statement word order.
  • Reported commands: tell/ask + person + to (or not to).
  • however and therefore open a sentence with a comma; due to takes a noun.

Vocabulary

False friends, punctuation and characters, social media and advertising, text types and persuasive devices.
